title: Edit isolated history and verify persistence
goal: Separate in-memory command history from its on-disk record without touching learner history.
challenge: Create an isolated history containing two harmless commands, remove only the obsolete entry, persist the result and reopen it in a separate child. Demonstrate that clearing memory alone does not clear disk.

steps.command: w=$(mktemp -d "$HOME/local-history.XXXXXX") && cd "$w" && pwd && here() { case "$w" in "$HOME"/local-history.??????) ;; *) return 19;; esac; test "${w%/*}" = "$HOME" && test -d "$w" && test ! -L "$w" && test "$(realpath -e "$w")" = "$w" && test "$(stat -c %U:%a "$w")" = learner:700 && test "$(pwd -P)" = "$w"; }; fresh() { for f; do test ! -e "$f" && test ! -L "$f" || return 19; done; }; here
steps.explanation: Create a unique learner-owned guest workspace; stop on error and record its absolute path. Reopening boots the disk, not these shell variables. Never use the host terminal.
steps.expected: A new private directory; no pre-existing files are changed.

steps.command: here && fresh history.txt && { env -i HOME="$w" PATH=/usr/bin:/bin HISTFILE="$w/history.txt" HISTSIZE=20 HISTFILESIZE=20 bash --noprofile --norc -c 'set -o history; history -c; history -s "printf obsolete"; history -s "printf retained"; history -w; unset HISTFILE; history' ; }
steps.explanation: These are inserted history strings, not executed commands. History is enabled explicitly in a noninteractive child for a reproducible demonstration. After the explicit save, unset HISTFILE only inside this child so its exit cannot save the list again.
steps.expected: Two entries persisted; parent history unchanged.

steps.command: here && { env -i HOME="$w" PATH=/usr/bin:/bin HISTFILE="$w/history.txt" bash --noprofile --norc -c 'history -c; history -r; history -d 1; history -w; unset HISTFILE; history' ; }
steps.explanation: Read the isolated file, inspect indexes, delete the observed obsolete entry and write the revised list. Real interactive indexes need inspection; do not assume a global history number.
steps.expected: Only printf retained remains in this fixture.

steps.command: here && { env -i HOME="$w" PATH=/usr/bin:/bin HISTFILE="$w/history.txt" bash --noprofile --norc -c 'history -c; history -r; history; history -c; test -s "$HISTFILE"' && cat history.txt; }
steps.explanation: Reopen in a new process. history -c affects memory; history -w is what rewrites the file. Default interactive exit behavior is separate from this explicitly written example.
steps.expected: Disk still contains the retained command after memory clear.

hints: Writing and appending history differ; this lesson uses -w deliberately.
Disk Resume does not restore a shell history list in RAM.
review: I retained actual output and checked the required contents, metadata or identity, not just command success.
I can explain the stated limitations, demonstrate the incorrect case, preserve originals and clean up only my recorded workspace.
coverage: LPIC-1 v5.0 partial 103.1. Self-reviewed and unscored: the application does not inspect guest results. No full-objective or exam-readiness claim.
